instructions: Fill a large pot with 4 quarts of water, add 1 tbsp of the salt and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, snap the woody ends off the asparagus and cut the spears into 2 inch pieces. Mince the 4 garlic cloves.
Zest the lemons until you have 1 tbsp, then squeeze them until you have 1/4 cup of juice. Chop the parsley leaves until you have 1/3 cup, and finely grate the Parmesan.
If the 1.25 lb shrimp aren't peeled and deveined, do that now. Pat them dry with paper towels and sprinkle them with 1 tsp salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper.

Add the 12 oz spaghetti to the boiling water and cook it until it's al dente, following the package time. Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta water, drain the spaghetti, then put it back in the pot with the lid on.

While the pasta cooks, heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large, deep skillet over medium high. Add the asparagus and the last 1/4 tsp salt and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's bright green and just tender. Tip it onto a plate.

Add the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil and 2 tbsp butter to the same pan. When the butter foams, lay the shrimp in a single layer and leave them for 1 minute, until the undersides turn pink. If they don't all fit in one layer, cook them in two batches.

Flip them, scatter in the garlic and cook the other side for 1 minute, stirring the garlic around, until the shrimp are pink all over. Cut one in half to check. It's done when it's opaque all the way through. Any longer and they turn tough.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the lemon zest, the 1/4 cup lemon juice and the parsley.
Add the spaghetti and the asparagus and toss everything together with tongs. If it looks dry, add the pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce coats the noodles.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the Parmesan and the 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes on the side.
method_notes: Natasha's Kitchen (the lead) cooks asparagus first in butter and oil, then the shrimp in the same pan with garlic, and stirs in lemon zest, lemon juice and parsley off the heat with no wine. Once Upon a Chef starts with shallots, reduces white wine by half, and builds the sauce with 6 tbsp butter and pasta water before the shrimp go back in. Both say to pull the shrimp the moment they turn opaque. This one follows the lead's method, uses 12 oz pasta and 1.25 lb shrimp so it fills four plates, puts the garlic in after the flip so it doesn't burn, and moves the chili flakes to the table.
